escalation_triggers: competing options in the ticket vs the earlier Unique Scans to Case Claims percentage card's recorded decision
escalation_note: The fast pass recommended best-of-N. The driver did NOT fan out 3 candidates. Reason: the residual uncertainty is a PRODUCT decision (whether to overturn the earlier Unique Scans to Case Claims percentage card's reviewed metric choice), which no additional prep candidate can settle; fanning out would delay reaching the human who must answer it. Instead the driver closed the fast pass's two contract gaps itself — the missing `exhaustiveness` section (swept inline) and the grep backstop — and is parking at the gate. If the answer to Q1 is 'yes, change the metric', the Phase 3 plan arbiter runs on this prep-context as normal.
synthesis: The card 'Unique Scans to Case Claims' currently renders pre_claim / deduped * 100 -- a genuine percentage (~99.7% for the reporter's month): the share of billed case claims whose vehicle an Insight camera had already scanned before the claim. DEV-2584 reports this as a display bug and asks for a numeric ratio, Unique Scan Counts / Unique LPR Case Claims (1,160,041 / 352 ~= 3,295.57). That is NOT a formatting change: it swaps the numerator from `pre_claim` (claims with a prior scan) to the org-wide unique-scan count, drops the *100, and drops the '%'. It redefines what the card measures. The code supplies a genuine argument on BOTH sides, which is why this parks for a human.
evidence_for_the_change: Family convention: the two sibling cards the ticket names as correct both compute unique_scans / denominator, format number_format(x, 1) with no '%', and describe themselves as 'scans per repo' / 'scans per LPR repo'. UniqueScansToRepo.php:316, UniqueScansToLprRepossession.php:248.

UniqueScansToRepo's own docblock (lines 41-47) tabulates all three cards and marks this one as the odd one out: 'UniqueScansToCaseClaims  vehicles / vehicles -- an honest <=100% rate' against the other two's 'unique scans / X'. The codebase already knows this card does not match its name's family.

Both siblings were built AFTER the earlier Unique Scans to Case Claims percentage card (the Unique Scans to Repo card and the LPR Repossessions funnel card), so the ratio convention is the newer, and currently dominant, reading of 'Unique Scans to X'.
evidence_against_the_change: The earlier Unique Scans to Case Claims percentage card built the percentage deliberately, on Oscar's explicit wording. That earlier investigation's ticket notes -- 'Option 1 was "96.6% of claimed vehicles were seen by our cameras first" -- a rate.'

That earlier work measured the ratio reading and was told not to build it. ticket.md:28-30 -- 'distinct scan_id / deduped claim triples | 119,364 / 11,975 | 9.97x -- not a rate' followed by 'Do not build the 9.97x reading.' The metric DEV-2584 asks for is that same not-a-rate family, with an even larger numerator.
The percentage survived a multi-round adversarial review and a pinned AC (96.6% fleet-wide, Jul 2026). Nothing in the DEV-2584 bundle acknowledges that decision or argues it should be reversed.
ruled_out: REGRESSION READING (checked and rejected): the earlier Unique Scans to Case Claims investigation journal records that a ClickHouse LEFT-JOIN default-fill trap would have inflated this card from 96.6% to exactly 99.7% -- the number the reporter observed. That coincidence made a live regression the leading alternative explanation. It is NOT the cause: the guard is present in the shipped query at app/Clickhouse/Queries/UniqueLprCaseClaimsQuery.php:371 (`h.hotlist_id != 0 AND h.first_scan < toDateTime(oc.claim_ts)`), and a 99.7% reading is unremarkable for the reporter's 352-claim month. The card is computing what it was built to compute.

questions.q: Should this card's metric change from a rate (share of case claims with a prior scan) to a ratio (unique scans per case claim)? The earlier Unique Scans to Case Claims percentage card built the rate deliberately on Oscar's explicit wording and its record says 'Do not build the 9.97x reading' -- the same not-a-rate family DEV-2584 now asks for. Against that, both sibling 'Unique Scans to X' cards are ratios and their docblock already flags this card as the odd one out.
questions.answer: YES — change it to the ratio. Build unique scans / case claims, no '%'. Rationale: the card's name and both sibling cards already mean 'unique scans per X', and UniqueScansToRepo's docblock flags this card as the family's odd one out. Worth confirming with Oscar since the rate was his ask, but the family convention has moved since that earlier percentage-card work.

questions.q: If the metric changes: 1 decimal place (both siblings' convention) or 2 (the ticket's 3,295.57 example)?
questions.answer: 1 decimal place — number_format($ratio, 1), matching both sibling cards. The ticket's 2dp example (3,295.57) was illustrative arithmetic, not a formatting spec.

questions.q: If the metric changes: does the existing 'X% of claimed vehicles were seen by our cameras first' rate survive anywhere -- a separate card, a tooltip line, a follow-up ticket -- or is it dropped entirely? It was an explicit operator ask in the earlier Unique Scans to Case Claims percentage-card work.
questions.answer: Drop it, no follow-up ticket. The UniqueLprCaseClaimsQuery::*WithPreClaimScans() methods stay in the codebase and stay tested, so the rate can be revived cheaply if anyone misses it.

questions.q: Is the observed 99.7% a regression of the earlier Unique Scans to Case Claims percentage card's documented LEFT-JOIN default-fill trap (which inflated the card to exactly 99.7%)?
questions.answer: No. The guard is present in the shipped query at UniqueLprCaseClaimsQuery.php:371 (`h.hotlist_id != 0 AND h.first_scan < toDateTime(oc.claim_ts)`), and 99.7% is an unremarkable value for the reporter's 352-claim month. The card computes what it was built to compute.

questions.q: Do the sibling cards establish that 'Unique Scans to X' means unique scans per X?
questions.answer: Yes. UniqueScansToRepo.php:316 computes unique_scans / total_repos and describes it as 'scans per repo'; UniqueScansToLprRepossession.php:248 computes unique_scans / dbRepos as 'scans per LPR repo'. Both format number_format(x, 1) with no '%'. UniqueScansToRepo's docblock (41-47) tabulates the three cards and names this one as the exception.

questions.q: Does the fix need a new ClickHouse round trip, and is that a scale risk?
questions.answer: No new cost -- it is a net reduction. The numerator reuses ScanPlateStatsBatchQuery's shared cache namespace, already populated by three other cards. The denominator drops the clarity.hits_cold join the pre_claim computation requires, taking the card's cold-key cost from the docblock's 106.8M read_rows / 3,828 MiB down to the base funnel's ~39.9M -- the cost UniqueLprCaseClaims already pays. Note it does NOT read UniqueLprCaseClaims's cached value: buildWidgetCacheKey() is class_basename-prefixed, so the denominator is fetched independently.

questions.q: Should the now-uncalled UniqueLprCaseClaimsQuery::*WithPreClaimScans() methods and their dedicated tests be removed?
questions.answer: Not in this ticket. CLAUDE.md's smallest-coherent-change rule argues against a same-PR removal outside the stated scope; they stay in place and tested, recorded under out_of_scope as a cleanup with no follow-up ticket yet.
